original_question: Characterize the Banach spaces with the Lebesgue property, meaning those spaces X for which every Riemann integrable function f: [0, 1] → X is continuous almost everywhere.
target_in_paper: Section 3.1 (Riemann integral), Problem 3.1: "Characterize Banach spaces having the LP."
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly asks for a characterization problem, identifies the property as the Lebesgue property, and gives the same defining condition used in the paper: every Riemann integrable function f:[0,1]→X is continuous almost everywhere.
missing_details: The paper works throughout with real Banach spaces.

The continuity in the definition is norm continuity; this should be stated explicitly, since the paper immediately distinguishes it from the weak Lebesgue property (WLP), where only weak continuity a.e. is required.
"Almost everywhere" is with respect to the Lebesgue measure on [0,1], as fixed in the notation section.
The official formulation in the paper is an open problem stated as "Characterize Banach spaces having the LP," where LP abbreviates "Lebesgue property."
To stay paper-faithful, it helps to note that this is the full characterization problem itself, not one of the nearby partial implications or examples.
refined_question: Characterize the real Banach spaces X with the Lebesgue property (LP), i.e. those for which every Riemann integrable function f:[0,1]→X is norm-continuous Lebesgue-almost everywhere on [0,1].
justification: The draft matches Problem 3.1 exactly rather than a broader neighboring question. In Section 3.1, the paper first defines the Lebesgue property by saying that a Banach space X has LP if every Riemann integrable function f:[0,1]→X is continuous a.e., and then states the open problem "Characterize Banach spaces having the LP." The notation section supplies the hidden assumptions needed to make the question stand alone: the paper considers only real Banach spaces, and [0,1] is equipped with Lebesgue measure. The same nearby passage also distinguishes LP from the weak Lebesgue property introduced immediately afterward, so norm continuity should be made explicit. The surrounding context records partial evidence—every asymptotic ℓ1 Banach space has LP; LP implies every spreading model is equivalent to the usual basis of ℓ1; and the Schur property alone does not suffice—which confirms that the intended target is the full characterization problem for LP itself.
